title: Coordinate Laplacian on Fourier coefficients
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates. The Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the function obtained by subtracting the average over the two possible values of coordinate $i$ from $f$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ if $i\in S$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is real-valued on the sign cube of dimension $n$
